title: Morgan Robertson's Wreck of the Titan foretells the Titanic

for, though it was April, the salt air was chilly

Seventy-five thousand tons--dead-weight--rushing through the fog at the rate of fifty feet a second, had hurled itself at an iceberg.

plain: Jesse Michels tells, more than once, of Futility, or the Wreck of the Titan, a short novel by Morgan Robertson published in 1898, about 14 years before the Titanic sank. In it the biggest liner ever built, the Titan, "considered practically unsinkable" and carrying too few lifeboats, hits an iceberg in the North Atlantic on an April night ("Ice ahead. Iceberg. Right under the bows"), and the writer Eric Wargo, author of a book on premonitions called Time Loops, tells it the same way. They bring it up as a possible case of someone sensing the future before it happened.

MANSFIELD" and "Copyright, 1912, by MORGAN ROBERTSON"; the tellers speak of the 1898 book, and the wording of the 1898 first edition is not checked here and may differ from the 1912 text quoted.
